                    ### Question
                    A 37-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being attacked with a knife. Physical examination shows a 4-cm laceration in the midline of the right forearm. An MRI of the right arm shows damage to a nerve that runs between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles. Loss of sensation over which of the following areas is most likely in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Palmar surface of the little finger
opb. Lateral aspect of the forearm
opc. Fingertip of the index finger
opd. Medial aspect of the forearm
ope. Dorsum of the thumb

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the scenario of a knife attack resulting in a laceration in the midline of the right forearm, the nerve most likely affected is the median nerve, which runs between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles. Damage to the median nerve typically results in loss of sensation at the fingertip of the index finger. This aligns with the consensus that the median nerve provides sensory innervation to the palmar surface of the thumb, index, middle, and part of the ring fingers. The retrieved evidence paths, while broad, confirm the involvement of nerves in the limb and hand structures, supporting the focus on the median nerve. Other options, such as the ulnar nerve affecting the little finger or the radial nerve affecting the dorsum of the thumb, are less likely given the location of the injury and the specific nerve path described. Therefore, the most likely area of sensory loss in this patient is the fingertip of the index finger.
